_doc: Calibration queries for the bounds of the two-stage normalization. They replace the hardcoded list of 29 in app/retrieval/calibrate.py, which is too small for a stable percentile (P5 of 29 samples is almost the minimum) and covers only 6 of the 8 departments with a corpus.
_in_domain_note: Written by hand from the list of courses that have a corpus (40 documents, 8 departments). They are not taken from the benchmark, so the normalizer does not adapt to the data it is evaluated on.
_ood_note: The out-of-domain probes are kept apart from data/rads_sample/ood_subset.jsonl, which measures out-of-domain refusal, and avoid its topics: cooking, sports, film and music, travel, health, shopping and gadgets, weather, gossip and politics, games, cars, and campus facilities.
_ood_selection_note: Eleven candidate probes were replaced after their scores were measured, because the curriculum covers them: personal branding on LinkedIn (top-1 cosine 0.7097), resigning from a job, job application letters, interview questions, fresh-graduate pay, vehicle insurance claims, health insurance premiums, term versus whole life insurance, mortgages, notary fees for a house sale, and subsidized versus commercial housing. The corpus holds Financial Management, Business Mathematics (annuities and insurance mathematics), Principles of Marketing, and Introduction to Management. Marking these topics out of domain would raise the out-of-domain ceiling and close the gap between the two sets. The replacements come from handicrafts, traditional arts, animal husbandry and farming, and folk tales, which touch none of the eight departments.
